meta.note: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Barkpark Unified Aesthetic. HAND-EDIT THIS FILE ONLY. Every surface token (Studio CSS vars, web @theme, Go semrole/taskboard artifact, paper-surface.css, pdrender) is GENERATED from here by W1.2 emitters — never edit generated output; regenerate it. Language-neutral: colors are HSL channels (H S% L%) so per-surface emitters can convert and the '/ alpha' soft-tint machinery + WCAG gate survive.
meta.colorFormat: HSL channels 'H S% L%' (no hsl() wrapper) so emitters can splice into hsl(<channels> / <alpha>) for soft tints
meta.outOfScope: emitters, drift gate, surface adoption (W1.2 / W2+)

_convention.form: Each role has { light, dark } as HSL channels. softAlpha derives status soft-tint fills: hsl(<role channels> / <softAlpha[theme]>).

TWO variants because the surface is theme-swapped two different ways with DELIBERATELY divergent hairlines: 'surface' = the shared paper-surface.css tokens the EDIT surfaces (Studio + the embedder bundle) stamp via html[data-theme] (emitted by paperBlock into the GENERATED marker region on the html[data-theme=light|dark] + bare-fallback selectors); 'reader' = the bulldocs.html.heex /papers reader-skin overrides (emitted by bulldocsBlock), which theme-swap via prefers-color-scheme and DIVERGE on --paper-rule (solid #dde7e2 light / rgba(231,237,233,0.13) dark) vs surface's rgba(21,33,29,0.09) / rgba(231,237,233,0.10) so the reader hairline reads cleaner on the article ground. reader.light stamps 7 roles; reader.dark re-skins 10 (it also owns ink-faint/chrome-bg/chrome-border the reader inherits from the shared light fallback). --paper-font-* and the callout --bp-tone-* are NOT here — fonts stay hand-authored in paper-surface.css, callouts are ts-w2's paperCallout family. GROUND (task-ddb1e0ab09a62466, 2026-09-02): reader.bg is the PAGE — bulldocsBlock emits body:has(.bp-paper-article){background:var(--paper-bg)}, the same token Studio's .bp-paper-surface paints — and bg-deep is the FILL tone (pre, inline code, .bp-stat, .bp-card, .bp-chart, .bp-heat, img frame, figure). The audit measured every fill at delta-L 0 while the body painted bg-deep; a light pair must keep delta-L >= 2% between the two (fjord #f6fbfd/#e7f0f2 ~3.5%, dark #050a0c/#0c1417 ~2.5%). measure_parity_test.exs pins both shells to one ground var.

chrome._note: UI chrome scale (Inter). Studio / web / TUI status text.

reading._note: Prose scale on the paper surface (serif). headingWeight is the SHARED heading weight (h1-h3) and validate.mjs pins it at 600 — it never moves. A step may declare its own optional `weight` (integer 100-900); it emits as --tok-reading-<step>-weight and the surface bridges it onto --bp-<step>-weight, so one level can take a different voice without the shared scalar moving (device 3, charter D29: h2 goes big-and-LIGHT — ~2.0x body at 400). letterSpacing is in em and emits as --tok-reading-<step>-tracking; a step without one inherits `normal`. The h1/body ratio is the EDITORIAL SCALE and validate.mjs floors it at 2.0 — a display size that only whispers above the prose is the defect this scale was retuned to fix.

air._note: The AIR scale for the paper reader: how much room an EVIDENCE block takes before it starts. Sourced from the benchmark artifact tooling/paper-excellence/evidence/erasure.html, whose own stylesheet measures code 24px, table 30px, asciicast 32px, callout 34px, stat tiles 36px, figure 40px against a ~22px unit. What is stored here is the RATIO, not the pixel: evidence opens at 1.1-1.85x that unit, so retuning `beat` moves the whole scale together and the law survives the number. RULED 2026-09-02 (task-741e0de1ddb3a482, closing the deferral this note used to carry): `beat` is the ARTIFACT'S AIR UNIT, not anybody's paragraph beat, and the ladder stays anchored on it. The reader's prose rhythm STAYS at `--bp-para-margin-top: 12pt` (16px), owned by type.reading. The name `beat` is kept because renaming an emitted token ripples through emit/check/validate and every generated artifact for zero pixels — what was wrong was the WORD, not the number, so the word is corrected here and everywhere the doctrine is written down. WHY 16 AND NOT 22: the ladder's bottom rung is code at 1.1 x 22 = 24.2px. At a 16px prose beat the step from a paragraph to the evidence it introduces is 8.2px — a step a reader can see. At 22 it would be 2.2px, invisible, and paragraph-to-paragraph (22) would then exceed heading-to-paragraph (16), inverting a heading's pull on its own first paragraph. 16px is also 0.556 of the 28.8px line, inside the classical half-line-to-full-line window. The relation is asserted, not remembered: tooling/paper-excellence/rig/shoot.mjs measures the RENDERED prose beat against the RENDERED code air per cell and reds unless the prose beat stays a clear step below it. Emitted as `--tok-air-*` by design/emit.mjs; every ratio here MUST have a consumer (validate.mjs floors the ordering, and a token with no consumer is the defect pe-w1-reader-editorial-typography was built to stop repeating).

section._note: The SECTION BOUNDARY: what separates one section of a paper from the next, and how the next one's head is drawn. Sourced from the benchmark artifact tooling/paper-excellence/evidence/erasure.html, whose `section { margin-bottom: 92px }` and `.sec-head { border-top: 2px solid var(--ink); padding-top: 16px }` are two halves of ONE device — the air says a section ended, the rule says the next one begins, and either alone reads as an accident. Barkpark has no element to hang them on: a `section` BLOCK flattens into its children, and a paper's real boundaries are its level-2 headings (all 51 h2s across the six rig fixtures follow non-heading content — not one is an h1/h2 stack). So both halves ride the `h2` element rule that View and Edit already share, which is also the only shape ProseMirror's flat heading node can mirror. `beat` is a RATIO of `space.air.beat`, for the reason the air ladder is: retune the beat and section rhythm moves WITH the evidence rhythm instead of drifting from it (4.18 x 22px = 91.96px, the artifact's 92). `rule` and `gap` are px — a hairline is a hairline at any beat, and `gap` is the artifact's `.sec-head` padding-top, the air between the rule and the words. There is deliberately NO fourth token for the artifact's `.sec-head .label` eyebrow: that needs a slot INSIDE the head, which neither the flat ProseMirror h2 node nor the reader's div-wrapped block stream can carry today (see the h2 rule in paper-surface.css). Emitted as `--tok-section-*` by design/emit.mjs and bridged onto `--bp-section-*`; every value MUST have a live consumer (check.mjs Part L), and the RENDERED gap is asserted against the artifact's 92px by tooling/paper-excellence/rig/shoot.mjs, so the calibration cannot rot into a number nobody can see.

rule._note: The RULE LADDER: a paper draws horizontal lines at exactly TWO weights, and the difference between them is the whole hierarchy. `space.section.rule` (2px) is the STRUCTURAL weight and is spent on one thing only — the head of a section. `hairline` is everything else: a table's header underline, a divider, a component's own frame, the terminal player's control bar. Sourced from the benchmark artifact tooling/paper-excellence/evidence/erasure.html, which draws 59 horizontal rules and spends the heavy weight on 8 of them — 6 `.sec-head` openings and the 2 edges of its closing `.declaration` frame — with every other line at `1px solid var(--rule)`. Barkpark's reader had drifted: a table header underline was 2px, a card's top accent 3px, a button's frame 2px, so a `bp-table` in the middle of an argument drew a line as loud as the boundary between two arguments and the reader could no longer tell structure from chrome by weight. Emitted as `--tok-rule-hairline` by design/emit.mjs and bridged onto `--bp-rule-hairline` on both surfaces; check.mjs Part M censuses BOTH arms (every stylesheet declaration and every rendered page), and validate.mjs floors the ladder so a hairline that grows to meet the structural weight is a decision rather than a typo.

evidence._note: The EVIDENCE BAND: how wide a block that improves with width is allowed to grow when it steps OUT of the prose column. Prose holds its reading measure (the 660px column, 66-72 characters per line); a table, a stat strip, a chart or a figure is not prose and is starved by it, so it breaks out to a wider centered band. Sourced from the benchmark artifact tooling/paper-excellence/evidence/erasure.html, whose `--wide: 1040px` against a `--measure: 66ch` prose column is the 1.58x ratio this reproduces (1040 / the reader's 660px column). What ships is a LAW, not a literal: the band takes `fill` of the available inline space, floored at `band`, capped at `bandMax`, and never crossing `gutter` at either edge — so it is CONTINUOUS in viewport width with no breakpoint to drift. `band` is the artifact's number and is where the band sits from ~1120px of available width up to `band / fill` (1600px); above that it grows to `bandMax`. Deliberately NOT a media query: the band is expressed in `100cqw`, which resolves against the Studio editor's content pane where one exists and against the viewport in the reader where none does, and a viewport @media beside a container-relative width would disagree inside the editor. `caption` is the reading measure a figcaption returns to INSIDE a wide figure — a caption is prose and never rides the band. It is in `ch`, and `ch` is the advance of the DIGIT ZERO, not the mean character advance: at the caption font (system-ui sans, 0.9rem, italic) the artifact’s literal 72ch renders 653px and holds 91-102 MEASURED characters per line, well past the 66-72 the prose beside it keeps. So the value is calibrated to the measure that actually lands rather than copied: 50ch renders 453px and 64-71 CPL on the same captions. The rig asserts the rendered number, so the calibration cannot rot. Emitted as `--tok-evidence-*` by design/emit.mjs and bridged onto `--bp-evidence-*` in paper-surface.css; every value here MUST have a live consumer (check.mjs Part K), and validate.mjs floors the ordering so a flattened or unreachable band is a decision rather than a typo.

elevation._note: Shadow ladder. Values are the LIGHT-theme shadows; dark is retuned per surface by emitters (deeper, lower-alpha). Recorded as CSS box-shadow strings.

lifecycle._note: Task-lifecycle vocabulary — the 7-state graph (task-lifecycle-visibility epic). RECONCILED 1:1 with internal/semrole/semrole.go (taskLifecycleRoles) + internal/taskboard (theme.go colors, components.go StatusGlyph, spinner.go asciiGlyph/frames, board.go life* consts). Pre-open thought states: considering (◌, a candidate just named) → researching (◎, under investigation) → open (ready to work). READY IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED: 'ready' shares the stored value 'open' (open + deps-met); the board overlays it. role '' = neutral/uncoloured (never a guess). 'color' here is the taskboard glyph hue (adaptive light/dark) and is INDEPENDENT of the semantic status palette above — notably 'done'/'closed' use TEAL, distinct from status.ok GREEN, and 'researching' uses a bespoke VIOLET that is not a status token. Emitters that need the semantic role tone read color.status via 'role'. The ◌ considering glyph collides with instanceLifecycle.provisioning — RULED accepted (disjoint vocabularies).

_default._note: unknown lifecycle degrades to the neutral dot

in_progress._escalation: board-only: warms info -> warn -> danger as the 5-min claim lease burns

done._color_note: TEAL — deliberately distinct from status.ok green (#10b981/#34d399). Finished work recedes.

considering._color_note: dim ~35% — a candidate the strategizer just named; fainter than open (still weighing whether it is real). Ladder extends DOWNWARD: thought is dimmer than backlog. Role '' (neutral) — the dotted circle is the glyph voice, not a status hue. The ◌ glyph collides with instanceLifecycle.provisioning; RULED accepted (disjoint vocabularies — task lifecycle vs cloud instance state).

researching._color_note: VIOLET — a candidate under active investigation (considering → researching). Deliberately distinct from every existing lifecycle hue (blue in_progress / amber blocked / teal done / neutral open) so 'being looked into' reads at a glance. Role '' (neutral): violet is a bespoke glyph hue like ready/open/cancelled carry, NOT a semantic status role (there is no violet status token).

instanceLifecycle._note: Cloud INSTANCE lifecycle vocabulary (charter azure-hetzner Decision 7). Seven states an operator sees on a Barkpark instance, dual-emitted to the SPA (.bp-inst--<state> glyph-tone classes) and the Go CLI/TUI chrome (GenInstanceLifecycle in internal/semrole/chrome_gen.go). Entry shape mirrors a task-lifecycle entry (role + glyph + codepoint + asciiGlyph) with ONE deliberate difference: there is NO bespoke color. Each state's colour is READ THROUGH its semantic status role, so identity never doubles as status (Decision 7) and the status palette stays the single state voice. role maps: live→ok, degraded→warn, decommissioned→danger, provisioning/adopted→info, stopped/archived→'' (neutral → the muted-text tone). A later wave rewires app.js statusPill/bucketOf + the CLI table renderers onto these consts; THIS slice only DEFINES + EMITS.

_default._note: unknown instance state degrades to the neutral dot
